title: HIVE Doctor — Abuse recognition & victim support
author: Jeff
review_status: UNVERIFIED — requires safeguarding / clinician sign-off before real-world use
safety: Protective, victim-facing only. Validates, keeps people safe, and signposts real confidential help. Contains NO methods that could enable abuse or grooming. For anyone who may be a minor, always points to a trusted adult and a child helpline and never encourages secrecy.
danger_msg: If you are in immediate danger, call your local emergency number now, or get to a safe place (a neighbour, a shop, anywhere with people) and call from there. Your safety comes first. You deserve to be safe.
resources_note: These are examples — most countries and regions have their own free, confidential helpline. This app works offline, so if you can get online, searching 'domestic abuse / sexual assault / child protection helpline' plus your area will find a local one. Contacting a helpline does not commit you to anything; they listen and help you decide.

categories.title: You deserve to be safe — support for abuse at home
categories.validation: What you're describing is abuse, and it is not your fault. You deserve to feel safe and respected. Abuse (hitting, threats, controlling what you do, money, or who you see) often repeats and can escalate — reaching out for support is a strong, sensible step.
markers: being controlled — your money, phone, friends or where you go
being put down, blamed or made to feel afraid
feeling you have to 'walk on eggshells'
steps: Think about a safe place you could go and one person you trust to tell.
If you can, keep ID, keys, some money and important papers somewhere you can grab quickly.
Agree a code word with someone so they know to get help.
You can talk to a confidential helpline to make a plan at your own pace — you don't have to decide anything today.
resources: Immediate danger: your local emergency number.
US: National Domestic Violence Hotline 1-800-799-7233 (text START to 88788).
Canada (Ontario): Assaulted Women's Helpline 1-866-863-0511.
UK: National Domestic Abuse Helpline 0808 2000 247.

triggers: made me have sex when i didnt want to
categories.title: What happened was not your fault — support after sexual assault
categories.validation: I'm really sorry this happened. It was not your fault, whatever the circumstances. You deserve support and care. What you do next is your choice, and help is available at every step.
markers: any sexual contact you did not freely agree to
being pressured, tricked, threatened or unable to consent
steps: If it was recent, medical care can check for injuries and offer protection against infection and pregnancy — this is available whether or not you involve police, and you can bring someone with you.
If you think you might want the option of reporting later, a specialist service can explain how evidence can be kept — but reporting is entirely your choice.
A confidential helpline can talk it through with you, at your pace.
resources: Immediate danger or serious injury: your local emergency number.
US: RAINN National Sexual Assault Hotline 1-800-656-4673.
UK: Rape Crisis 0808 500 2222.
Canada: contact a local sexual assault / domestic violence care centre or 211.

categories.title: This isn't okay, and it isn't your fault — getting help
categories.validation: You're right to feel uneasy, and you're doing the right thing by looking for help. What you're describing is not okay and it is NOT your fault. A safe adult should never ask you to keep secrets from your parents or carers, give you gifts for secrecy, try to get you alone, ask for photos, or make you feel you'd be in trouble for telling.
markers: an adult asking you to keep secrets from your parents or carers
being offered gifts, money or special attention for secrecy
someone trying to get you alone or to meet privately
being asked for photos or sent things that make you uncomfortable
being told it's your fault or that you'd get in trouble if you tell
steps: Tell a trusted adult as soon as you can — a parent, carer, teacher, school counsellor, or another adult you trust.
You will not be in trouble for telling. Keeping it secret is what the other person wants, not what's best for you.
If anyone has hurt you or you don't feel safe, you can contact a free, confidential child helpline — they are used to helping with exactly this.
resources: Immediate danger: your local emergency number.
US: Childhelp National Child Abuse Hotline 1-800-422-4453.
Canada: Kids Help Phone 1-800-668-6868 (text CONNECT to 686868).
UK: Childline 0800 1111 / NSPCC 0808 800 5000.

categories.title: Helping a child who may be being harmed
categories.validation: Thank you for taking this seriously — that protects the child. If a child tells you something, stay calm, believe them, let them know it's not their fault and that they did the right thing telling you. Keep them safe and don't confront the suspected person yourself.
markers: unexplained injuries, fear of a particular person, or a big change in mood or behaviour
age-inappropriate knowledge, or secrecy around an adult
withdrawal, or going back to younger behaviours
steps: Write down what was said as soon as you can, using the child's own words.
Report to your local child protection service or the police — they will guide you.
Get support for yourself too; it's hard to hear.
resources: A child in immediate danger: your local emergency number.
US: Childhelp 1-800-422-4453.
Canada: your provincial child protection services / Kids Help Phone 1-800-668-6868.

categories.title: You deserve to be treated with safety and respect
categories.validation: Being hurt, neglected, or having your money taken is abuse — including by family or carers — and it is not your fault. You have a right to be safe and to be treated with respect.
markers: being hurt, handled roughly, or left without food, warmth, hygiene or care
money, pension or belongings being taken or controlled
being frightened, threatened or ignored by someone who cares for you
steps: Tell someone you trust outside the situation — another relative, a GP, or a social worker.
A confidential helpline can explain your options and what support exists.
resources: Immediate danger: your local emergency number.
US: Adult Protective Services / Eldercare Locator 1-800-677-1116.
UK: Hourglass 0808 808 8141.
Canada: your local Adult Protective Services or 211.

closing: You are not alone, and none of this is your fault. Talking to someone does not commit you to any action — it just means you don't have to carry it by yourself.
